verdict.rationale: Svelte's own GitHub description says it compiles components into JavaScript that directly and surgically updates the DOM, so the UI is made of real DOM nodes. One hands-on community report describes stepping through readable compiled component code while profiling, which implies browser-side debugging works. Svelte's docs never describe a devtools debugging workflow, so that half of the story rests on a single community anecdote. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of debugging in browser devtools, explicit evidence of inspecting the rendered DOM nodes there, and broader independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug my UI directly in browser devtools because the framework renders real DOM nodes

citations.quote: converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM
The generated code is readable: they stepped through compiled component code while profiling a layout-per-frame issue and traced it to their own function.
Effects run after the DOM updates and can return teardown functions.
